title: Stitchboard: Route & Model Snapshot UI prototype + chart specs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, high-density 'Stitchboard' snapshot view for per-route and per-model performance. The view should be embeddable in route and model detail pages and optimized for quick diagnostics: latency percentiles, throughput, token flow, error rates, and cost attribution. Deliverables: Figma prototype (desktop + compact mobile), annotated chart specs for engineering, accessibility pass, and review notes.
background: Current console views are tile-heavy and require multiple clicks to get a high-level sense of model or route health. Platform teams need a single glance surface that surfaces both short-term SLO slippage and longer-term cost trends for routing decisions and incident triage.
goals: Create a single-pane snapshot that shows latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (rps or requests/min), token counts (input/output), and cost per 1k tokens
Make the component embeddable in route and model pages with consistent layout and sizing
Enable instant drilldown to the timeline and token-waterfall views
Keep visual density high but preserve legibility and accessibility
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates desktop and compact modes
Chart spec doc lists axes, data windows, aggregations, tooltip content, and alert thresholds
Design tokens specified (colors, spacing, type scale) and match console system
Prototype passes a basic accessibility check (color contrast and keyboard focus)
Engineering can implement the view without custom backend metrics beyond existing telemetry
wireframe_notes: Top row: small-status summary (SLO, recent error trend, cost delta) in 3 microcards
Middle left: latency ribbon showing p50/p95/p99 as stacked area with donut-style percent-over-slo
Middle right: throughput sparkline with request-per-minute heat indicator and workload badge
Bottom left: token flow miniature waterfall (input -> generation -> cache-hit savings) with hoverable tooltip per-token cost
Bottom right: compact cost breakdown bar (model compute vs embedding vs fixed) with % change compared to baseline
Hover states: all mini-charts show a focused tooltip and link to a dedicated timeline view
Embedding in route page uses a 3/4 width card; embedding in model page uses full-width, but same spacing rules
chart_specs: Latency Ribbon: stacked percentile area chart showing p50 (base), p95 (mid), p99 (top); x-axis: time (configurable 1h/6h/24h/7d), y-axis: latency ms, aggregation window 1m, tooltip shows absolute ms and % over target SLO

Throughput Sparkline: line chart of requests/min with translucent gradient for density; overlay markers for autoscale events; y-axis adaptive (linear), tooltip shows request count and 1-minute avg latency

Token Waterfall Mini: horizontal waterfall showing median token split: prompt tokens, generated tokens, kv-cache hits (negative cost), and estimated cost segment per bucket; values shown in tokens and estimated $/1k tokens
Cost Attribution Bars: stacked bar showing compute vs embedding vs network per selected interval; supports toggling to show normalized cost per 10k tokens
Error Rate Micro: small discrete band with banded shading showing error percentage and exact counts on hover; threshold color switches at 0.5% and 2%
SLO Gauge: compact radial with numeric percent and small sparkline; color-coded green/amber/red with accessible labels
data_contract_notes: Expect time-series endpoints to provide percentile series (p50/p95/p99) and sample counts with same timestamps
Throughput needs bucketed counts at 1m resolution for last 24h and 1h for recent zoom
Token waterfall expects per-request summary fields: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_callbacks indicating cache hits
Cost calc should be client-side derived from per-model unit-cost metadata (provided by pricing service)
interactions: Clicking a microcard navigates to full timeline with pre-filtered route/model and time window
Hover timeline shows vertical crosshair and snaps p50/p95/p99 values
Inline 'compare to baseline' control toggles a faded baseline series
Compact mode collapses charts into accordions for narrow widths
Export CSV button on bottom-right exports current chart payloads and computed cost breakdown
visual_tokens: Primary palette: console-blue #0B61FF for p50; accent-amber #FFB020 for p95; critical-red #E12D3A for p99
Background neutral: #0F1720 card surface; text-primary: #E6EEF8; subdued: #9FB0C8
Microcard icons: line weights 2px, 16px icon size
review_feedback: PM: prefer p95 over median as prominent latency indicator for SLAs (Arjun) - adjust microcard order
Eng: confirm that percentile series are available at 1m resolution; if not, provide 5m fallback (Priya)
SRE: add an annotation band for recent incidents and link to on-call runbook (Carlos)
Data: prefer pre-aggregated token waterfall payload to avoid heavy client transforms (Hannah)
decisions: Use percentile ribbon instead of separate p50/p95/p99 smallcharts to conserve vertical space
Implement cost calc client-side using pricing metadata to avoid backend churn
Compact mobile mode will prioritize SLO + throughput microcards and collapse token waterfall into a tappable detail
next_steps: Address engineering feedback about data resolution and update chart_specs accordingly (owner: Liam)
Run a 30-minute design review with PM/SRE/Data to finalize microcard ordering (owner: Maya)
Produce annotated handoff doc for frontend with exact CSS vars and responsive breakpoints (owner: DesignOps)
Schedule a feasibility spike with runtime team to validate telemetry endpoints (owner: Priya)
notes: Aim for a first pass implementation that reuses existing chart components to speed delivery
Keep the Stitchboard component composable so it can be surfaced in dashboards, alerts emails, and Slack snippets
Consider A/B testing color thresholds during rollout to assess operator attention and false positive rate
